fixed.explanation: In the single-block case, BlockManager.fast_xs returns a view of one row of the 2D block values. When df.loc[row, cols] first takes the columns (creating a large temporary array), the tiny row Series holds a reference to that whole temporary. Copying the row in fast_xs makes the result independent and releases the large base.

query.intent: DataFrame.loc/iloc row selection with a list of columns on a single row builds a Series from a block's 2D values as a view (e.g. fast_xs / _ixs / BlockManager.fast_xs), so the resulting small Series references the large parent array. It should copy or avoid holding the base array when taking a row cross-section.
query.symptom: Selecting a single row with a list of columns returns a small Series that is a view keeping the large underlying array alive, causing memory growth (regression in pandas 3.0).

history.analysis: Results shown are unrelated to row cross-section. The likely location is BlockManager.fast_xs in pandas/core/internals/managers.py, or DataFrame._ixs / _getitem_lowerdim in indexing.py, where a single row is taken with a column list (via take/reindex on columns).
